note: Editorial overview only. No procedure steps, quantities or doses are given; every therapy here must be performed or supervised by a qualified practitioner. Chapter locators are chapter-level and unverified against a recorded edition.

items.name: Panchakarma
items.summary: A planned course of purification (Shodhana) built around Vamana, Virechana, Basti, Nasya and Raktamokshana (Sushruta) or two kinds of Basti (Charaka), preceded by preparatory oleation and sudation (Purvakarma) and followed by a graded diet (Samsarjana Krama).
indications: Chosen by the physician according to the dosha involved, the patient's strength (Bala) and the season
contraindications: Children and the very elderly unless specifically adapted by a specialist
Acute illness, fever, severe weakness, dehydration
Uncontrolled heart, kidney or liver disease
risks: Dehydration and electrolyte disturbance after emesis or purgation
items.aftercare: Graded return to normal diet under supervision; rest; avoid exertion, cold exposure and daytime sleep as advised.
items.practitioner: BAMS/MD physician with Panchakarma training, in a centre equipped to manage complications.
items.evidence: Small trials exist for some conditions; overall quality of evidence is low and protocols vary widely between centres.

sources.text: Charaka Samhita, Sutra Sthana 15 (Upakalpaniya) and Siddhi Sthana 1 (Kalpana Siddhi)

items.name: Snehana
items.summary: Internal (Snehapana) or external (Abhyanga) use of medicated fats. Internal oleation is a preparatory step before Shodhana and is done only under supervision.
indications: Preparation for Vamana or Virechana
Vata disorders (as decided by the physician)
contraindications: Obesity and high blood lipids (internal oleation)
risks: Rising blood lipids with high-dose internal fat
items.aftercare: Warm water, light food; do not combine with self-directed purgation.
items.practitioner: Internal oleation: physician only. Gentle external oil massage is part of ordinary daily routine.

items.name: Abhyanga
items.summary: Application of warm oil to the body as part of Dinacharya (daily routine) or as a therapeutic massage.
indications: Daily routine for general wellbeing
Dry skin; Vata-predominant states
contraindications: Deep vein thrombosis or unexplained leg swelling
risks: Slips and falls on oily floors
items.aftercare: Warm bath after a short interval; avoid cold wind.
items.practitioner: Self-massage is generally safe; therapeutic massage by a trained therapist.
items.evidence: Massage in general has modest evidence for short-term relaxation and pain relief; Ayurveda-specific evidence is limited.

items.name: Swedana
items.summary: Induced sweating by steam, heated boluses, warm poultices or other methods, usually after oleation.
indications: Stiffness, heaviness and cold-predominant pain (as decided by the physician)
Preparation for Shodhana
items.aftercare: Rest in a warm room; rehydrate; avoid cold exposure.

items.name: Vamana
items.summary: Planned, induced vomiting to eliminate Kapha, preceded by oleation and sudation. Never a home procedure.
indications: Selected Kapha-predominant disorders, decided by a specialist
contraindications: Bleeding from upper digestive tract, hernia, recent surgery
Eye disorders such as glaucoma (raised pressure)
items.aftercare: Graded diet (Samsarjana Krama) and rest under supervision.
items.practitioner: Panchakarma specialist in an equipped centre.

items.name: Virechana
items.summary: Planned purgation to eliminate Pitta, preceded by oleation and sudation.
indications: Selected Pitta-predominant disorders, decided by a specialist
contraindications: Inflammatory bowel disease, rectal bleeding, diarrhoea
risks: Dehydration, low potassium, low blood pressure
items.aftercare: Graded diet (Samsarjana Krama) and rest under supervision.

items.name: Basti
items.summary: Medicated decoctions (Niruha / Asthapana) or oils (Anuvasana) given rectally, the principal procedure for Vata disorders. Charaka describes Basti as half of all treatment.
indications: Selected Vata-predominant disorders, decided by a specialist
contraindications: Rectal bleeding, fissure or recent anorectal surgery (as judged by physician)
Diarrhoea, intestinal obstruction, inflammatory bowel disease
items.aftercare: Rest; light, warm food.
items.evidence: Small trials in some musculoskeletal and neurological conditions; low-quality evidence.

items.name: Nasya
items.summary: Medicines instilled through the nose for disorders of the head and neck. Light daily nasal oil (Pratimarsha) is part of the classical daily routine; therapeutic Nasya is a physician-directed procedure.
indications: Selected disorders of head, nose, throat and neck, decided by a physician
contraindications: Immediately after meals, bathing or drinking alcohol
risks: Aspiration of oil into lungs (lipoid pneumonia) with repeated or excessive use
items.aftercare: Avoid cold wind and cold water; gargle with warm water.

items.name: Raktamokshana
items.summary: Removal of blood by leeches (Jalaukavacharana), venepuncture (Siravyadha) or other methods; Sushruta counts it among the five Shodhana procedures.
indications: Selected skin and blood-borne (Rakta) disorders, decided by a specialist
contraindications: Anaemia, bleeding disorders, anticoagulant or antiplatelet medicines
items.aftercare: Wound care and observation for bleeding and infection.
items.practitioner: Shalya specialist with sterile technique; never a home procedure.
items.evidence: Medicinal leech therapy has a recognised role in some reconstructive surgery; evidence for Ayurvedic indications is very limited.

items.name: Shirodhara
items.english: Continuous pouring of liquid on the forehead
items.summary: A steady stream of warm oil, milk, buttermilk or decoction poured over the forehead. It is a later practice tradition (prominent in Kerala) rather than a procedure described in detail in the Brihat Trayi.
indications: Used in practice for stress, sleep difficulty and headache (decided by the physician)
items.aftercare: Keep the head warm; wash oil out after the advised interval.
items.evidence: A few small trials for insomnia and anxiety; low-quality evidence.

items.name: Kati Basti
items.english: Warm oil pooled on the lower back
items.summary: Warm medicated oil retained over the lower back inside a ring of dough. Despite the name it is an external therapy, not an enema; it belongs to later practice tradition.
indications: Chronic low back pain without warning signs (decided by the physician)
contraindications: Back pain with fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel changes or leg weakness (seek urgent care)
items.aftercare: Avoid cold exposure and heavy lifting the same day.

items.name: Janu Basti
items.english: Warm oil pooled over the knee
items.summary: As Kati Basti, applied to the knee joint. External therapy from later practice tradition.
indications: Chronic knee pain such as osteoarthritis (decided by the physician)
contraindications: Hot, red, swollen joint or fever (possible infection or gout: seek medical care)
items.aftercare: Avoid cold exposure.

items.name: Udvartana
items.summary: Massage with herbal powders in the direction opposite to hair growth, described in the daily routine for reducing Kapha and Meda.
indications: Kapha-predominant states and excess body fat (as part of a wider plan)
items.aftercare: Warm bath.

items.name: Kshara Karma and Kshara Sutra
items.summary: Application of caustic alkaline preparations, or a medicated thread (Kshara Sutra) tied through a fistula track. Kshara Sutra for anal fistula has been studied in clinical trials, including ICMR-supported work.
indications: Anal fistula, haemorrhoids and some skin growths, decided by a Shalya specialist
contraindications: Inflammatory bowel disease, tuberculosis or cancer-related fistula (need specialist care)
items.aftercare: Regular dressing and review by the surgeon.
items.practitioner: Shalya Tantra specialist (MS Ayurveda) in a surgical setting. Never self-applied.
items.evidence: Kshara Sutra for fistula-in-ano has comparatively better evidence than most Ayurvedic procedures, including randomised comparisons with conventional surgery.

items.name: Agnikarma
items.summary: Controlled application of heated instruments to a small area of skin, described by Sushruta for persistent pain and some lesions.
indications: Selected cases of persistent localised pain, decided by a specialist
contraindications: Diabetes with neuropathy, poor circulation, bleeding disorders
items.aftercare: Wound care as instructed.
items.practitioner: Shalya specialist; never a home procedure.

items.name: Pizhichil
items.summary: Warm medicated oil squeezed continuously over the body while it is massaged; a Kerala practice tradition combining Snehana and Swedana.
indications: Selected Vata disorders (decided by the physician)
items.aftercare: Rest; warm bath; light food.

items.name: Shirobasti
items.summary: Warm medicated oil is retained on the scalp inside a leather or rexine cap sealed at the forehead, for a set time. A form of Murdhni Taila (oil on the head).
indications: Selected Vata disorders of the head, sleep difficulty and facial palsy, decided by a physician
risks: Chill, oil running into the eyes, neck strain
items.aftercare: Keep the head covered and warm; wash out the oil after the advised interval.

items.name: Netra Tarpana
items.summary: Medicated ghee is held over the open eyes inside a ring of dough, a classical Kriyakalpa (eye procedure).
indications: Dry, strained eyes and selected eye disorders, decided by an eye specialist (Shalakya)
contraindications: Eye infection, conjunctivitis, recent eye surgery
Glaucoma or any painful red eye (needs ophthalmology)
items.aftercare: Avoid bright light, wind and screens for the rest of the day.
items.evidence: Small studies in dry eye; low-quality evidence.

items.name: Putapaka
items.english: Eye treatment with expressed herbal juice
items.summary: Juice prepared by a special roasting process is retained over the eyes, usually after Tarpana, as an eye Kriyakalpa.
indications: Selected eye disorders, decided by a Shalakya specialist
items.aftercare: Protect eyes from light and wind.

items.name: Kavala and Gandusha
items.english: Gargling and holding liquids in the mouth
items.summary: Gandusha is holding a liquid (oil, decoction, milk) in the mouth without moving it; Kavala is swishing a smaller amount. Part of daily routine and used for oral disorders.
indications: Oral hygiene as part of daily routine
Mouth ulcers, gum disease and dry mouth, alongside dental care
contraindications: Children who may swallow or choke
Acute severe oral infection (see a dentist)
risks: Aspiration if done lying down; swallowing medicated liquids
items.aftercare: Spit out completely; rinse with warm water.
items.practitioner: Self-care for simple oils; physician for medicated liquids.
items.evidence: Oil pulling has small, low-quality studies on plaque and gingivitis; it does not replace brushing and flossing.

items.name: Karnapurana
items.summary: Warm oil is filled into the ear canal for a short time; described in daily routine and for some ear disorders.
indications: Daily routine in classical texts; selected ear complaints decided by a physician
contraindications: Ear discharge, ear infection or ear pain with fever
risks: Infection, burns from hot oil, worsening of undiagnosed perforation
items.aftercare: Keep the ear dry and warm.
items.practitioner: Have the ear examined first; do not use with any discharge.

items.name: Lepa
items.summary: A paste of herbs is applied to the skin, usually against the direction of hair growth, and removed before it dries completely.
indications: Local swelling, pain and some skin conditions, decided by a physician
contraindications: Toxic ingredients (for example Bhallataka) on sensitive skin
risks: Contact dermatitis, burns from irritant herbs
items.aftercare: Wash off gently; watch for rash.

items.name: Upanaha
items.summary: A warm herbal poultice bandaged over a painful or stiff area, sometimes left overnight; a form of Swedana.
indications: Stiff, painful joints and muscles (Vata), decided by a physician
contraindications: Hot, red, swollen joints (possible infection or gout)
Broken skin, reduced sensation, diabetes with neuropathy
items.aftercare: Remove and clean the skin; avoid cold exposure.

items.name: Pinda Sveda (Njavarakizhi)
items.summary: Boluses of herbs or of rice cooked in milk and herbal decoction (Njavarakizhi, a Kerala practice) are heated and massaged over the body.
indications: Selected Vata disorders with wasting or stiffness, decided by a physician
contraindications: Heart disease and high blood pressure (whole-body treatment)
items.aftercare: Rest, warm bath, light food.
